key_insight: Ionic concentration gradients reorganize supramolecular polymers into spatially distinct zones where local composition directly controls local assembly dynamics, creating quasi-equilibrium behavior across the gradient.
engineering_relevance: This suggests gradients can be used as a design knob to program where synthetic soft materials assemble, disassemble, or become dynamically active in space and time.
method: Two prototypical supramolecular polymer models under imposed ionic gradients
evidence_signal: The abstract reports molecular-resolution simulations showing pronounced spatial reorganization and locally enhanced supramolecular activity under gradients, with local dynamics largely matching local concentrations.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on simulation models, so translation to real materials will depend on whether the coarse-grained interactions and imposed gradient conditions faithfully capture experimental systems.
paper_title: Ionic gradients shape the spatial organization and dynamics of supramolecular polymers
